Section 1 of 13

If Salvation Is Free, Why Does Obedience Matter?

Imagine someone risks everything to rescue you from a dangerous situation. You would not pay that person back by returning to the danger. You would trust the one who saved you and listen when that person warned you about what could destroy you.

Jesus rescued us from the guilt and power of sin. We cannot earn that gift.

What happens after we receive it?

The Creator invites us to trust Him enough to follow His way.

Obedience does not purchase His love. Obedience grows from knowing that He already loves us.

Read John 14:15 ↗.

Jesus said, “If you love Me, keep My commandments.”

He connected obedience with love.

Obedience Is a Response to Grace

Read Ephesians 2:8–10 ↗.

We are saved by grace through faith. Good actions cannot save us.

The same passage says we were created to do good works. Grace does not leave us where it found us. It restores our relationship with the Creator and teaches us how to live.

The order matters:

The Creator loves you.

Jesus saves you.

You trust Him.

The Holy Spirit changes you.

Obedience grows from that relationship.

We do not obey so the Creator will accept us. We obey because He has accepted us through Jesus.

The Creator’s Law Begins With Freedom

Read Exodus 20:1–17 ↗.

Before God gave the Ten Commandments, He reminded Israel that He had rescued them from slavery.

He did not begin by saying, “Obey Me so I might rescue you.”

He began by saying, “I rescued you. Now let Me teach you how free people live.”

The Ten Commandments protect our relationship with the Creator and with one another.

The first four commandments explain how to love God:

  1. Worship the Creator alone.
  2. Do not make or worship idols.
  3. Treat the Creator’s name with honor.
  4. Remember the seventh-day Sabbath.

The final six commandments explain how to love other people. We will explore those in the next guide.

What Is the Purpose of God’s Law?

The Creator’s law reveals His character.

God is faithful, so His law teaches loyalty.

God is truthful, so His law condemns lying.

God gives life, so His law protects life.

God is generous, so His law condemns stealing and greed.

God is pure, so His law protects faithfulness in relationships.

God respects freedom, so His law rejects control, exploitation, and harm.

Read Psalm 19:7–11 ↗.

God’s law is described as perfect, trustworthy, right, and more valuable than gold.

The law is not a weapon for powerful people to control everyone beneath them. Jesus strongly confronted leaders who used religious rules to burden others while excusing their own wrongdoing.

Read Matthew 23:1–4 ↗ and Matthew 23:23 ↗.

God’s law applies to leaders and ordinary people alike. No pastor, government, institution, nation, or family stands above it.

Can the Law Save You?

Read Romans 3:20 ↗.

The law reveals sin, but it cannot forgive sin.

A mirror can show that your face is dirty, but the mirror cannot wash your face. In the same way, God’s law shows what is wrong, but only Jesus can cleanse and forgive us.

Read Romans 7:7 ↗ and 1 John 1:9 ↗.

The law helps us recognize sin. Jesus provides forgiveness. The Holy Spirit gives us power to begin living differently.

Trying to keep the commandments without Jesus produces pride, fear, frustration, or hidden sin.

Receiving grace while knowingly rejecting the Creator’s commands also damages our relationship with Him.

Grace and obedience belong together in the right order.

Did Jesus Remove the Ten Commandments?

Read Matthew 5:17–19 ↗.

Jesus said He did not come to destroy God’s law. He came to fulfill it.

To fulfill the law means that Jesus lived it perfectly, revealed its true meaning, and completed what Scripture had promised about Him. It does not mean that He made dishonesty, murder, adultery, idolatry, or other sins acceptable.

Read Matthew 22:35–40 ↗.

Jesus summarized the law in two great commands:

Love the Creator with your entire being.

Love your neighbor as yourself.

This summary did not replace the Ten Commandments. It explained their foundation.

The first four commandments show what love for God looks like. The last six show what love for other people looks like.

Read Romans 13:8–10 ↗.

Love does not remove the law. Love fulfills it because real love does not harm another person.

The First Commandment: Give the Creator Your Highest Loyalty

Read Exodus 20:2–3 ↗.

God says that we should have no other gods before Him.

This commandment is about loyalty.

The Creator gave you life. Jesus gave His life to rescue you. No person, spirit, object, institution, or ambition deserves the place that belongs to Him.

An idol does not have to be a statue. Anything that controls your decisions or becomes more important than the Creator can take His place.

Possible idols include:

  • Money
  • Success
  • Popularity
  • A romantic relationship
  • Personal appearance
  • Political power
  • Substances
  • Entertainment
  • A spiritual leader
  • Family approval
  • Your phone or online identity
  • Your own desires

These things may not all be wrong by themselves. They become idols when loyalty to them becomes greater than loyalty to God.

Ask yourself:

“What am I most afraid to lose?”
“What has the greatest influence over my choices?”
“What do I turn to first when I feel empty?”

Your answers may reveal what holds the highest place in your life.

Does Loyalty to the Creator Mean Rejecting Your People?

The Creator does not ask you to stop loving your family, community, or nation.

Read Mark 7:9–13 ↗ and 1 Timothy 5:8 ↗.

The Bible teaches us to honor and care for our families. Following Jesus should make us more faithful, compassionate, truthful, and dependable.

At the same time, no family, culture, or community should take the Creator’s place.

Every person eventually faces moments when loyalty to God conflicts with the expectations of other people. This can be painful.

Read Acts 5:29 ↗.

The Creator asks for your highest loyalty, but He does not teach you to become proud, hostile, or disrespectful. You can disagree with someone while continuing to treat that person with dignity and love.

Following the Creator may change some of your choices. It does not require shame about your ancestry or rejection of your people.

The Second Commandment: Do Not Reduce the Creator to an Image

Read Exodus 20:4–6 ↗.

The second commandment warns against creating an image and treating it as God.

The Creator is greater than anything human hands can make. No statue, picture, symbol, object, animal, or part of creation can contain Him.

Images can influence how we think. If we reduce God to an object, we may begin treating the object as if it carries divine power.

Creation points toward the Creator, but creation should not receive the worship that belongs to Him.

Read Romans 1:20–25 ↗.

People throughout the world have sometimes replaced the Creator with something He made. The form differs among cultures, but the spiritual danger is the same.

This commandment also warns us against trying to control spiritual power through objects or rituals. The Creator is a Person to know and trust. He is not a power we can own, carry, or manipulate.

What About Honoring Those Who Came Before Us?

Remembering family members and respecting those who came before us is different from worshiping them.

You can value the sacrifices, stories, wisdom, and lessons passed down through your family. Scripture itself remembers faithful people from earlier generations.

Read Hebrews 11:1–40 ↗.

However, the Creator asks us to direct prayer and worship to Him alone. We should not seek spiritual guidance, protection, or hidden knowledge from those who have died.

Later guides will examine what the Bible teaches about death and the spirit world.

The Creator welcomes your prayers directly. You do not need another spirit to carry your words to Him.

Read Hebrews 4:14–16 ↗.

Through Jesus, you can approach God with confidence.

The Third Commandment: Honor the Creator’s Name

Read Exodus 20:7 ↗.

God’s name represents His character, authority, and reputation.

Using His name carelessly includes more than speaking it in anger. It also includes claiming to represent Him while living in a way that misrepresents His character.

A person takes God’s name in vain when that person:

  • Uses religion to gain power
  • Claims God’s approval for cruelty
  • Makes promises in God’s name and breaks them
  • Uses spiritual authority to manipulate others
  • Speaks about God with no intention of following Him
  • Publicly claims faith while secretly practicing harm

People have sometimes used the Creator’s name while doing things that directly opposed His law of love. That is a serious violation of the third commandment.

Read Ezekiel 36:22–23 ↗.

God cares about how His name is represented.

If you carry His name, treat people in a way that helps them see His honesty, mercy, justice, and love.

The Fourth Commandment: Remember the Creator’s Day

Read Exodus 20:8–11 ↗.

The fourth commandment calls us to remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy.

The Creator identifies the Sabbath as the seventh day. He established it at creation, long before any modern nation or religious denomination existed.

Read Genesis 2:1–3 ↗.

God rested on the seventh day, blessed it, and made it holy.

The Sabbath reminds us that:

  • The Creator made us.
  • Our value does not come from constant work.
  • Time with God matters.
  • Rest is a gift.
  • Everyone deserves freedom from endless labor.
  • We depend on the Creator for life.

The biblical seventh day begins at sunset on Friday and continues until sunset on Saturday.

Read Leviticus 23:32 ↗ and Mark 1:32 ↗.

The Sabbath will receive a full guide later in this series. For now, notice that the command begins with one important word:

“Remember.”

The Creator knew humanity would be tempted to forget.

What Does Wholehearted Love Look Like?

Read Deuteronomy 6:4–9 ↗.

The Creator wants more than one hour of attention each week. He wants to be part of your entire life.

Love for God influences:

  • How you use your time
  • What you do with your body
  • How you spend money
  • The relationships you pursue
  • The media you consume
  • The promises you make
  • The way you treat people
  • The goals you chase
  • The person you are when no one is watching

The Creator is not asking to become one small part of your life. He wants to guide every part because He knows what leads toward life.

The Creator Writes His Law on the Heart

Read Hebrews 8:10 ↗.

God promises to place His law within us and write it on our hearts.

This is more than memorizing rules.

The Holy Spirit changes what we want. We begin to see the Creator’s commands as protection and wisdom rather than interference.

Read Psalm 40:8 ↗.

A changed heart can say, “I delight to do Your will.”

You may not feel that delight in every situation. Obedience sometimes requires choosing what is right while your feelings pull in another direction.

As you continue walking with Jesus, trust grows. The Creator’s way becomes clearer, and obedience becomes a loving response instead of a fearful performance.

What If You Do Not Fully Understand a Command?

You can obey what you understand while continuing to learn.

Read John 7:17 ↗.

Jesus taught that a willingness to do God’s will helps us recognize whether a teaching comes from Him.

Sometimes we demand complete understanding before taking the first step. The Creator often gives greater understanding after we begin responding to the truth we already see.

This does not mean following people blindly. Test every teaching by Scripture.

It means becoming honest with God:

“Creator, if this is truly Your will, help me understand it and give me the courage to follow.”

What If Obedience Costs You Something?

Loyalty to the Creator may affect relationships, habits, work choices, or how you use your time.

Jesus never promised that following Him would always be easy.

Read Luke 9:23–25 ↗.

He did promise that nothing surrendered to Him is more valuable than the life He gives.

You may fear disappointing someone, losing an opportunity, or being misunderstood. Bring that fear to the Creator.

Ask for wisdom, courage, and a loving way to follow what is true.

Obedience may carry a cost. Disobedience also carries a cost, even when that cost is not immediately visible.

The Creator sees beyond the present moment. His instructions lead toward freedom and life.

Think About It

Write your answers in your own words.

  1. What is the difference between obeying to earn love and obeying because you are loved?
  2. Why did the Creator remind Israel of freedom before giving the Ten Commandments?
  3. What does God’s law reveal about His character?
  4. What person, desire, object, or goal most strongly influences your choices?
  5. Is there anything good in your life that may be taking the Creator’s place?
  6. How can someone misuse God’s name through actions?
  7. What does the Sabbath reveal about the Creator?
  8. Is there a command you find difficult to understand or follow?
  9. What would loving the Creator with your whole life change this week?

Try This During the Coming Week

Read one section of the first four commandments each day:

  • Day 1: Exodus 20:1–3 ↗
  • Day 2: Exodus 20:4–6 ↗
  • Day 3: Exodus 20:7 ↗
  • Day 4: Exodus 20:8–11 ↗
  • Day 5: Matthew 22:35–40 ↗
  • Day 6: John 14:15–24 ↗
  • Day 7: Psalm 19:7–14 ↗

After each reading, write down:

  • What does this passage show me about the Creator?
  • What does it reveal about love?
  • Is anything competing with God for first place in my life?
  • What one act of trust can I practice today?

Choose one daily habit that will help you place the Creator first. It may be praying before checking your phone, reading Scripture before beginning work, or setting aside quiet time to listen to God.

A Prayer You Can Pray

Creator God, thank You for saving me by grace. I know that I cannot earn Your love. Teach me to obey because I trust You and love You. Show me anything that has taken Your place in my life. Help me worship You alone, honor Your name, remember Your holy day, and bring every part of my life under Your direction. Write Your law on my heart through the Holy Spirit. Give me courage when obedience is difficult and help my life reveal Your character. Amen.

Remember This

Salvation is a gift that cannot be earned.

Obedience is a loving response to the Creator’s grace.

God gave His commandments to people He had rescued from slavery.

The law reveals sin but cannot forgive it.

Jesus forgives us and the Holy Spirit gives us power to obey.

The first four commandments teach us how to love the Creator.

God asks for your highest loyalty without erasing your Native identity.

His name should never be used to excuse control, cruelty, or abuse.

The seventh-day Sabbath honors the Creator and protects sacred time for worship and rest.

The Creator wants to write His law upon your heart.
